messages.subject: multiple tables in knitr
parts:
I've toyed a bit with knitr now, and it seems to work quite OK. I use Emacs and ess, and seem to be able to work around most of the peculiarities. There's one that has me stymied though. It seems that knitr's tables support is a little less streamlined than its figure support. 

I've been able to create graphics with captions and labels, and multiple graphics that share label and caption. No such luck with tables.

It seems that the 

<<label,fig.cap='Nice caption'>>=
... nice illo here ...
@

gives LaTeX a caption and a label, at least with hist, qqnorm and probplot. but not with xtable.

I'd like to have this:

<<label>>=
... one table ...
... another table ...
@

All in one table environment with caption and label. Is there a canonical way of doing this? 

Thank you,

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] multiple tables in knitr
parts:
The key to tables with knitr is the chunk option results='asis', and
you are right that tables are not as well supported as graphics. You
will have to go with a few more keystrokes if you want to put more
than one table in one table environment. Just remember if you use
packages like xtable to create tables, be sure not to generate the
code for the table environment (i.e. print(xtable, floating = FALSE)).
I do not recognize a "canonical" way for this.

If you use the latest development version of knitr
(https://github.com/yihui/knitr#readme), I have an experimental
function kable() that generates "barebone" tables, e.g.

\documentclass{article}

\begin{document}

\begin{table}
\caption{A tale of two tables.}
<<test, results='asis'>>=
library(knitr)
kable(head(iris))
kable(head(mtcars[, 1:5]))
@
\end{table}

\end{document}

Tables are not fun to work with, and that is probably the reason why
they have low priority in knitr :)

Regards,
Yihui
